SELECTED_INDEX: 1
CONFIDENCE: 0.35
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the typical pattern of an aliphatic alkene bearing a halogen.  
• Very strong C=C stretch at 1652 cm⁻¹ together with a vinylic C–H stretch at 3081 cm⁻¹ indicates an isolated C=C-H unit.  
• Intense CH stretches at 2908 and 2989 cm⁻¹ plus strong CH₃ bending at 1419/1395 cm⁻¹ point to several methyl groups.  
• Two prominent halogen-related bands are present: 767 cm⁻¹ (medium-strong) and 531 cm⁻¹ (medium).  Alkyl C–Cl stretches commonly appear in the 750-700 cm⁻¹ region (in-plane) and 600-500 cm⁻¹ region (out-of-plane), matching a chloroalkene better than a bromo compound.  
• Minor peaks at 842-893 cm⁻¹ and around 1015-1054 cm⁻¹ can be assigned to CH₃ rocking / C–C skeletal modes of a highly substituted alkene.  

Among the candidates only CC(C)=CCl (candidate 1) contains:  
– one vinylic CH (gives 3081 cm⁻¹),  
– multiple methyl groups (gives strong 2900–3000 and 1400 cm⁻¹ bands),  
– a single C=C bond (1652 cm⁻¹),  
– a C–Cl bond that can account for both 767 and 531 cm⁻¹ bands.  

Candidates without chlorine fail to explain the pair of halogen bands, while the dichloro or bromo structures lack the observed vinylic CH stretch or have additional heteroatom groups that should give extra strong bands (e.g. C=O, C–O) not seen here. Therefore candidate 1 best fits the experimental Raman data.
